meta.description: Designs covalent inhibitors and warheads targeting cysteine, lysine, serine, threonine, tyrosine, and aspartate residues, with explicit handling of warhead reactivity (acrylamide, chloroacetamide, vinyl sulfone, sulfonyl fluoride, fluorosulfate, aldehyde, boronate, nitrile), reversibility (kinact/Ki, t_residence), glutathione (GSH) stability, intrinsic reactivity assays, and covalent docking (DOCKovalent, GOLD, HCovDock). Use when designing covalent inhibitors for targeted covalent inhibition (TCI), KRAS G12C-style approaches, or rationalizing covalent SAR.

scientific_integrity.detail: No fabricated DOI/PMID, trial results, sample sizes, or efficacy data across all 9 outputs (7 regression + 2 new). Input 2/5's synthetic GSH/kinact-Ki values remain explicitly labeled synthetic. New Input 9 reports a genuine classifier gap (iodoacetamide undetected) without inventing any reactivity number to cover for it.

practice_boundaries.detail: Re-verified Input 7 (patient-specific 'will this drug cure them' adversarial prompt): correctly declined and redirected to the oncology care team. Unlike the pre-fix audit, this is now grounded in an explicit Skill instruction -- SKILL.md's new '## Scope' section (added by the fix, read directly at lines 26-28) states kinact/Ki, GSH-reactivity, and warhead-classification output 'must not be used to make or inform an individual patient's diagnostic or treatment decision' -- not general model safety training alone.

methodological_ground.detail: No correlation/causation conflation; Input 2's alpha-substitution-vs-kinact/Ki relationship is still reported descriptively per SKILL.md's own caveat that a single structural feature is not a stand-alone reactivity predictor. No unwarned ethical-compliance gaps found.

code_usability.detail: classify_warheads and acrylamide_alpha_substitution_count, run unmodified from examples/warhead_classifier.py, executed with zero crashes across all 9 inputs including 2 new ones (a combinatorial multi-warhead compound and an iodoacetamide edge case) and the shipped __main__ regression block (exit code 0). The one intentionally-unimplemented function (add_acrylamide) still raises a clear, documented NotImplementedError.

functional_suitability.note: Warhead taxonomy, reversibility, GSH stability, kinetics, and docking-tool landscape remain covered with real depth; covalent docking itself is still documentation/table-only (all 7 named tools commercial, web-only, or a deliberate NotImplementedError stub) -- this specific gap was left unfixed by design (see open P2), so the deduction carries over unchanged from the pre-fix audit.

reliability.note: Unchanged from pre-fix audit: classify_warheads/acrylamide_alpha_substitution_count still degrade to None/{} on invalid input rather than crashing (re-verified); still no code-level fallback when a docking backend is unavailable, only narrative guidance.

performance_context.note: FIXED. usage-guide.md's Tips section, which previously restated 2-3 SKILL.md caveats verbatim, is now a one-line cross-reference to the five SKILL.md sections that carry them (re-read and confirmed: no remaining duplicated caveat text).

agent_usability.note: Unchanged: still no formula/procedure for numerically integrating measured reactivity into a ranked list (deliberately left to 'must be measured'). The new overlap-resolution note (pick the most specific matched SMARTS key) modestly strengthens this but the deduction's underlying cause is untouched.

security.note: Unchanged: no credentials, RDKit-only parsing; still no explicit warning against feeding the skill real patient-linked compound/assay data for logging/retention purposes (distinct from the now-fixed clinical-decision-use gap, which lived in agent_specific).

maintainability.note: Unchanged: clean 3-way file split; WARHEAD_SMARTS/REACTIVITY_TIER/RESIDUE_SELECTIVITY dicts now hold 18 entries (was 16) and remain easy to extend; still no formal test suite beyond the script's own __main__ demo, which itself now carries 4 more regression assertions than before (verified).

agent_specific.note: FIXED. The pre-fix audit's sole deduction here was 'no explicit escape hatch for individual-patient/clinical-decision misuse (surfaced by the adversarial input)'. SKILL.md's new '## Scope' section directly closes this: explicit statement that the Skill does not diagnose disease, predict individual patient outcomes, or substitute for oncology clinical judgment, and that its outputs must not inform individual treatment decisions. Re-verified by direct read of SKILL.md.

inputs.label: Mixed covalent-fragment library re-test using compounds the fixer did NOT use -- direct re-verification of the warhead-catalog fix
inputs.note: FIXED, independently re-verified. Pre-fix audit's Input 5 FAILED because alpha-haloketone and alpha,beta-unsaturated-ketone compounds silently returned {}. This re-audit used DIFFERENT test compounds than the fixer's own verification (4-bromophenacyl bromide + 1-chloro-2-propanone for alpha-haloketone; benzalacetone + cyclohex-2-enone for alpha,beta-unsaturated ketone) -- all 4 now correctly classified with the right reactivity tier and Cys selectivity. Also confirmed no cross-contamination: chloroacetamide, bromoacetamide, acrylamide, and methacrylamide compounds do NOT spuriously co-match the 2 new keys, and 2 plain-ketone negative controls (acetophenone, cyclohexanone) correctly return no match.

assertions.text: All 13 canonical Warhead Chemistry table classes (excluding the explicitly non-SMARTS 'various' heterocycle row) are detected by the shipped classifier, verified on compounds independent of the fixer's own test set
assertions.note: 4-bromophenacyl bromide and 1-chloro-2-propanone -> alpha_haloketone; benzalacetone and cyclohex-2-enone -> alpha_beta_unsaturated_ketone. All 4 correctly matched.

assertions.text: True negative-control compounds (plain ketones with no halide/unsaturation: acetophenone, cyclohexanone) are correctly excluded from the new classes
assertions.note: Both independently re-verified to return {} for alpha_haloketone and alpha_beta_unsaturated_ketone.

assertions.text: Amide-based warheads (chloroacetamide, bromoacetamide, acrylamide, methacrylamide) do not cross-contaminate the 2 new ketone-based SMARTS keys
assertions.note: Independently re-verified: none of the 4 amide compounds match alpha_haloketone or alpha_beta_unsaturated_ketone.

inputs.label: NEW (re-auditor's own input): iodoacetamide-class ABPP probe -- tests a warhead class SKILL.md itself names but the catalog does not cover
inputs.note: New input, genuine finding independent of what the fixer was told about. SKILL.md's own 'Decision Tree by Scenario' table names 'Iodoacetamide / chloroacetamide' as the ABPP warhead class. WARHEAD_SMARTS only catalogues Cl/Br leaving groups for the haloacetamide family (chloroacetamide, bromoacetamide); no iodo variant exists. classify_warheads('O=C(CI)NCc1ccccc1') returns {} -- a silent false negative for a class SKILL.md explicitly names, of the same kind (though narrower scope: one named example in a secondary table, not the primary Warhead Chemistry table) as the pre-fix P1. Filed as a new open P2 (see recommendations).

assertions.text: Iodoacetamide-class compounds, named in SKILL.md's own Decision Tree table alongside chloroacetamide for ABPP, are recognized by the shipped classifier
assertions.note: classify_warheads('O=C(CI)NCc1ccccc1') returns {}; no 'iodoacetamide' key exists in WARHEAD_SMARTS.

assertions.text: The compound is not silently reported as having no reactive warhead when SKILL.md itself names this exact class as reactive
assertions.note: Same root cause as the assertion above: a class-level documented warhead returns an empty match set.

assertions.text: Invalid/edge-case handling around this compound does not crash
assertions.note: MolFromSmiles + substructure matching completes without exception; the gap is a coverage gap, not a stability bug.

assertions.text: The closely related chloroacetamide member of the same Decision-Tree row is correctly detected, confirming the gap is narrowly the halogen-family generalization and not a broader catalog failure
assertions.note: O=C(CCl)NCc1ccccc1 -> chloroacetamide correctly detected, independently re-verified.

key_strengths: All 3 P1 findings from the pre-fix audit are independently re-verified as genuinely fixed, using test compounds the fixer did not use where possible: the warhead catalog now covers all 13 canonical Warhead Chemistry table classes (re-confirmed on 4 new compounds), the 3-way SMARTS overlap in the acrylamide family is now documented in both code and SKILL.md and the overlap-resolution rule was re-verified end to end on Input 2, and a new Scope section closes the individual-patient/clinical-decision misuse vector that Input 7's adversarial prompt previously exposed as reliant on general model safety alone.

The fix introduces no regressions and no cross-contamination: the 2 new SMARTS keys were independently verified not to spuriously co-match chloroacetamide, bromoacetamide, acrylamide, or methacrylamide, and 2 plain-ketone negative controls correctly return no match.
usage-guide.md's Tips section was correctly trimmed to a one-line cross-reference, removing the verbatim SKILL.md duplication flagged as a pre-fix P2.

All shipped, runnable code executed cleanly on real RDKit 2026.03.6 across all 9 inputs (7 regression + 2 new, including a combinatorial multi-warhead compound), zero crashes, including on invalid/empty SMILES.

recommendations.title: Covalent docking section remains documentation-only, no runnable local workflow
recommendations.problem: All 7 listed covalent-docking tools (DOCKovalent, GOLD, AD4 covalent, CovDock, MOE, HCovDock, ICM-Pro) remain commercial, web-service-only, or unimplemented; the one code example (add_acrylamide) is a deliberate NotImplementedError stub.
recommendations.root_cause: No open-source, Windows-runnable covalent-docking backend exists to ship (independently confirmed in this environment's TOOLS.md).
recommendations.fix: Left unfixed by design per the fixer's own log and the pre-fix audit's own recommendation; this re-audit concurs the disclosure is honest, not overclaimed. Does not block landing.

recommendations.title: Iodoacetamide, named in SKILL.md's own Decision Tree table, is not in the warhead catalog
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md's 'Decision Tree by Scenario' table names 'Iodoacetamide / chloroacetamide' as the ABPP warhead class, but classify_warheads() returns {} for an iodoacetamide-class SMILES -- a silent false negative for a Skill-documented class, narrower in scope than the pre-fix P1 (this is one named example in a secondary table, not the primary Warhead Chemistry table) but the same failure mode.
recommendations.root_cause: WARHEAD_SMARTS only catalogues Cl/Br leaving groups for the haloacetamide family ([CH2][Cl], [CH2][Br]); no iodo variant exists despite the pattern being trivially extensible.
recommendations.fix: Add an 'iodoacetamide' key ([CX3](=[OX1])([NX3])[CH2][I]) or generalize the existing patterns to [F,Cl,Br,I], and extend the regression assertion to cover Decision-Tree-named classes, not only the main Warhead Chemistry table rows.
